content.user_title: Manage Git Workflows with Team Standards
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent commits, branches, and review habits to keep history readable. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a practical Git workflow checklist.
actual_capabilities: Defines Conventional Commit message format and accepted commit types.
Provides branch naming guidance using type, ticket ID, and description.
Explains GitFlow roles for main, develop, feature, release, and hotfix branches.
Lists auto-invoke triggers for commits, branches, merges, pull requests, and releases.
Provides a pre-commit checklist for secret scanning and quality gates.
limitations: Does not perform Git operations by itself.
Does not define hosting provider settings or repository permissions.
Does not replace project-specific release or deployment rules.
Does not resolve complex merge conflicts without repository context.

use_cases.title: Standardize Commit Messages
use_cases.description: Apply Conventional Commits to produce readable history and consistent changelog inputs.

use_cases.title: Plan Feature Branches
use_cases.description: Choose clear branch names and GitFlow paths before starting collaborative work.

use_cases.title: Prepare Safe Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check staged changes for secrets and run quality gates before review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and suggest one Conventional Commit message with a short explanation.

prompt_templates.title: Name a Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a branch name for this task using the type, ticket ID, and description pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pull request readiness checklist for my current changes using this Git workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Release Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the branch flow for a release or hotfix and identify which branches should receive the final merge.

output_examples.input: I fixed login validation and added tests.
output_examples.output: Suggested commit message: fix(auth): validate login input. Before committing, scan staged changes for secrets and run the project quality gates.

output_examples.input: We need a branch for ticket CORE-456 to fix a null pointer bug.
output_examples.output: Suggested branch name: bugfix/CORE-456-fix-null-pointer. Branch from the integration branch if this follows the standard GitFlow path.

output_examples.input: A production issue needs an urgent patch.
output_examples.output: Use a hotfix branch from main. Merge the completed fix back to both main and develop after review.

best_practices: Keep commit subjects short, specific, and written in the imperative mood.
Run secret checks and project quality gates before committing changes.
Use branch names that connect work type, ticket ID, and plain description.
anti_patterns: Do not mix unrelated work into one commit or pull request.
Do not push secrets, credentials, or generated tokens to version control.
Do not bypass review steps for normal feature or release work.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and checklist commands that the user or agent can review before use.

faq.question: Which commit style does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends Conventional Commits with a type, optional scope, and clear subject.

faq.question: Does it support GitFlow?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes main, develop, feature, release, and hotfix branch paths.

faq.question: Can it help with pull request preparation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide branch naming, commit cleanup, secret checks, and quality gate reminders.

faq.question: Is it tied to GitHub only?
faq.answer: No. The guidance is general Git workflow advice and can apply to many hosting providers.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
